headline: A focused 5-6 day birding safari can yield 250-300 species in the right location
summary: Meaningful birding is absolutely possible in under 7 days if the itinerary focuses on a single habitat-rich region rather than multi-destination hopping. Kenya's Rift Valley lakes (Naivasha, Baringo, Bogoria) or Uganda's forest corridor (Bwindi to Queen Elizabeth) can deliver 250-300 species in 5-6 days with a specialist guide. The key is eliminating transit days and maximizing dawn-to-dusk field time in species-dense locations.

assumptions.text: Single-region focus outperforms multi-destination travel for short birding trips.
A specialist birding guide adds 30-50 species to a short trip versus a generalist guide.
Maximum birding time (dawn to dusk) is essential for short trips to hit species targets.

gains: 5-6 focused days often outperform 10 scattered days for species count
Single region means no transit days lost to airports and long drives
Short trip forces prioritization of target species over completionism
Cost-effective way to test if Africa birding warrants longer return trip
losses: Miss habitat diversity available in longer multi-region itineraries
No buffer for weather disruptions or site closures
Cannot combine distant highlights (Serengeti + Bwindi requires 10+ days)
Exhausting pace with no rest days built in

change_conditions: If specific rare species are targets, verify they are reliably found in your chosen region.
If combining birding with Big Five, extend to 8-10 days for reasonable coverage of both.
If first Africa trip, consider 5-day birding focus + 2-day wildlife extension.
If traveling from Europe, jet lag may reduce effectiveness of days 1-2.
